query: Assess which LLM training experiments are feasible on a 5x NVIDIA CMP 170HX box (320 GB HBM2e, ~810 TFLOPS bf16, PCIe Gen2 x4, no NVLink, no P2P) and verify the repo's four supporting claims.
cross_gap_dependency: cc-1 is the master variable. The 88%-attention / 8.5x-6ND correction is the only thing that makes DDP overhead ~4% at 1M tokens, makes wall-clock the binding constraint, and makes the sparse-attention payoff ceiling 39-54%. If cc-1 lands a measured 32k/4k per-token cost ratio >= 0.4, then cc-2 (fabric numerator) and cc-6 (algbw vs busbw column) become decisive again, because the compute window shrinks toward the 6ND value and the repo's 36% / 54-58% overhead figures return to being the live question. Fetch cc-1 first; the other five are conditional on its outcome.
critic_notes: Arithmetic inconsistency the drafter will inherit: comparisons.md Tension 2 states the MoE DDP overhead is '252%, not 36% - exactly the total/active ratio'. That figure divides 18.7 s of communication (28 GB at 1.5 GB/s wire) by 7.41 s of 6ND compute at 810 TFLOPS. Under Locus 4's own correction the 32k compute window for a 1B-active/24L/2048 model is ~56 s at 450 TFLOPS, so the same payload is ~33%, not 252%. The 7x total/active multiplier is real as a ratio but is applied to an uncorrected denominator. This weakens the 'PP is the topology for the MoE' claim (PP 4-14% vs DDP ~33%, not 18x better) and is the specific thing cc-3 and cc-6 test.

The prompt's suggested #2 falsifier ('<0.4 GB/s') does not actually overturn #2. At 2.0 GB payload and 56.8 s of compute, 0.4 GB/s gives 8.8% overhead, 0.2 GB/s gives 17.6%, and only <=0.1 GB/s restores the repo's ~35%. cc-2 is therefore framed around the <=0.1-0.2 GB/s band, not 0.4.

The corpus contains no on-box training, all-reduce, NCCL, DDP, PP or ZeRO measurement at all (performancemd and club-170hx BENCHMARKS both say so explicitly). Every gap below that targets a hardware number is therefore asking for a T2 community measurement or a T1 user artifact, never a T3 arithmetic estimate.

gaps.target_position: #1 - the ~90-100 TFLOPS/card (450-500 aggregate) training denominator and the claim that 6ND is invalid at 32k because attention is 88% of step FLOPs and total FLOPs are 8.5x the 6ND estimate. Downstream this also carries #2's ~4% DDP overhead, #4's -39 to -54% sparse-attention payoff, and #5's 5-12 day wall-clock.
search_queries: long-context LLM training throughput tokens per second 32k versus 4k sequence length measured A100 1B model
Ring Attention Ulysses LoongTrain USP measured per-token training time versus sequence length scaling
attention wall-clock fraction of training step at 32k context profiler Megatron-LM context parallel 500M model
gaps.rationale: Four of the six committed positions are downstream of one arithmetic claim: that PaLM's 6N+12LHQT at 32k makes attention 88.3% of step FLOPs and total FLOPs 8.52x the 6ND estimate for a 494-500M/28L/2048 model. That claim is FLOP arithmetic, not wall-clock, and the corpus contains no measured 32k-vs-4k throughput ratio at all. Every long-context systems paper (Ring Attention, DeepSpeed Ulysses, LoongTrain, USP, Seq1F1B, Megatron-Core context parallel, ProLong) reports measured tok/s or ms/step at 32k-128k against a short-context baseline, and none is in the vault. If the measured per-token cost ratio at 32k is ~2-2.5x rather than 4.39x - because the 4k baseline is launch-bound at ~42% MFU while the 32k run amortizes better, or because the attention kernel runs closer to GEMM efficiency than the blended estimate assumes - then the 8.5x correction overstates the wall-clock penalty by ~1.8x, the throughput band moves from 9-22k to 16-40k tok/s, the 9B run is 2.6-6.5 days rather than 5-12, and DDP overhead at 1M tokens rises from 4.4% to ~9%. The report's central inversion ('wall-clock, not the fabric, is binding') survives qualitatively but loses its quantitative spine. The repo's own 140k tok/s / 494M datapoint is the tell: under 6ND it implies 84 TFLOPS/card (42% MFU, plausible); with attention counted at 4k it implies 163 TFLOPS/card (80% MFU, implausible). A measured curve settles which of the three repo numbers (140k tok/s, 494M, 'inferred ~4k') is wrong. Conversely, if the measured ratio is <=0.23, the position is confirmed and should be committed harder.
gaps.overturn_condition: A measured 32k/4k per-token training cost ratio >= 0.4 for a 0.5-1B dense model on A100/H100, or a profiler-measured attention-time fraction <= 50% of step time at 32k, or MLPerf/Megatron training logs on A100-40GB showing attention is not ~88% of step FLOPs at 32k for a 500M model.
gaps.evidence_tier_target: T2/T3 (measured on A100/H100; transfers by ratio, absolute throughput ~0.65x on 70 SMs at 250 W)

gaps.target_position: #2 - DDP overhead at 1M-token batches is ~4% after correction (not 36%), so the fabric is NOT the binding constraint; wall-clock is.
search_queries: nccl-tests all_reduce_perf 5 GPUs PCIe Gen2 x4 no NVLink algbw busbw 1GB message
NCCL all-reduce 5 ranks PCIe host staged SHM bandwidth measured
5 GPU PCIe ring all-reduce NUMA congestion penalty measured Tartan
gaps.rationale: The fabric half of the report rests on one unverified user self-report (0.75 GiB/s) that no corpus source corroborates at 5 ranks: every receipt is 2-4 ranks, and the corpus's own band (0.93-1.07 GB/s busbw, 0.58-0.67 GB/s algbw) is derived from a 3-card x16 host and a 2-card x4 P2P copy. A 5-rank, Gen2 x4, host-staged all_reduce_perf at 1-2 GB is the missing measurement, and the Tartan/TPDS warning that 5-GPU PCIe rings are pathological ('one should avoid adopting 5 GPUs') predicts the N=5 penalty exceeds the 1.6x ring-load factor. The threshold matters and the prompt's suggested 0.4 GB/s is too high: at 2.0 GB payload against 56.8 s of compute, 0.4 GB/s is 8.8% overhead and does not overturn anything. Only <=0.1 GB/s (35%) or <=0.2 GB/s with fp32 buckets (4.0 GB payload, 35%) restores a fabric-binding overhead and falsifies 'the fabric is not the binding constraint'. If it lands in that band, the report's central inversion is wrong and the repo's original framing was right.
gaps.overturn_condition: A 5-rank, Gen2 x4, no-P2P all_reduce_perf at 1-2 GB showing algbw <= 0.1 GB/s (or <= 0.2 GB/s with fp32 gradient buckets), i.e. a 5-GPU NUMA/ring penalty 3-5x worse than the 4-rank extrapolation.

gaps.target_position: #3 - 'DDP only' reframed as 'data-parallel only', with ZeRO-2 (33.6 GB state, DDP-identical 2-Psi) or PP=5 (25.8 GB/card, 4-14% bubble) as the two viable routes, and EP/TP excluded by the fabric.
search_queries: ZeRO-2 versus DDP step time PCIe no NVLink measured overhead 4x3090 8x4090
pipeline parallelism 32k sequence length PCIe no P2P throughput bubble measured 1F1B
expert parallelism training PCIe no NVLink host staged measured overhead MoE
gaps.rationale: This is the report's headline prescription and its least-measured claim: the locus itself rates the prescriptive half at only 50-80% because reduce-scatter throughput on this no-P2P fabric is unmeasured. Three specific measurements would break it. (a) A ZeRO-2-vs-DDP A/B on a PCIe-only no-NVLink box at >=1B params showing >50% step-time overhead. ZeRO-2's 'exactly 2-Psi' is a byte-volume identity, not a wall-clock one: it replaces one fused all-reduce with a reduce-scatter plus an all-gather, two kernel launches and a sync point, and on a host-staged fabric where every hop is two PCIe traversals the extra round trip can dominate. The corpus's own measured practitioner study (behind-the-scenes-of-distributed-training) already shows the dial flattening on a slow wire and ZeRO-1/2 losing ~20% of DDP even on a fast one - and its slow wire is 35 GB/s, ~45x faster than this box. (b) A measured 5-stage 1F1B PP step at 32k on a no-P2P box showing >60% overhead. The 4-14% bubble assumes the 134 MB hand-off hides inside a 243 ms compute window at 1.68 GB/s per direction; at an effective 0.5 GB/s under host-staged bounce-buffer contention the hand-off is 268 ms and PP becomes comm-bound. (c) A host-staged EP or TP training implementation at >=1B params showing <2x overhead, which would reopen the topology the report closes. If (a) and (b) both fail, the only viable route is the frozen-table design and the repo's original conclusion is restored - a direct reversal of Tension 2. Note also that the position's own 252% MoE figure is inconsistent with Locus 4's correction (it is ~33% at 56.8 s of compute, not 252%), so the PP-vs-DDP margin is far narrower than the report claims and a measured MoE DDP step would settle it.
gaps.overturn_condition: A measured ZeRO-2 or 5-stage PP step on a no-P2P PCIe fabric at >=1B params / 32k showing >50% overhead; or reduce-scatter throughput <= 1/3 of all-reduce throughput on host-staged PCIe; or a host-staged EP/TP training run at >=1B params with <2x overhead.
gaps.evidence_tier_target: T2 (community measurement on 3090/4090 PCIe) / T3 (systems-paper measurement on PCIe-only consumer GPUs)

gaps.target_position: #4 - CSA2 at 32k on sm_80 is a kernel-porting project, not an experiment; run NSA instead (6.3x fwd / 3.4x bwd at 32k).
search_queries: sparse MLA DSA backward kernel A100 sm_80 triton training implementation
StreamIndex TileLang sparse attention A100 sm_80 support backward kernel
native sparse attention NSA kernel end-to-end training speedup versus FlashAttention-2 32k A100
gaps.rationale: The Verdict's top lever is 'sparse attention (-39 to -54%)', and it rests on NSA's 6.3x/3.4x at 32k. Two sources would break it. (a) An sm_80 DSA/CSA2 training kernel that exists today - a Triton or CUDA sparse-MLA fwd+bwd tested on A100, or StreamIndex/TileLang/vLLM adding sm_80 backward support. The locus searched five stacks and found only vLLM's inference-only TRITON_MLA_SPARSE, but that is a fast-moving surface: FlashMLA dropped Hopper within one release, and a Triton backward is arch-portable in principle. If one appears, CSA2 becomes an experiment and 'drop CSA2' is wrong. (b) A measured NSA *end-to-end* training-step speedup at 32k against FlashAttention-2 on A100. The 6.3x/3.4x are module-level ratios, and if the baseline is a Triton full-attention kernel rather than FA2 (Triton attention typically runs 0.7-0.8x of FA2 on A100), the real end-to-end speedup could be 1.5-2x, which at an 88% attention share is a -10 to -20% step-time saving, not -39 to -54%. That would collapse the Verdict's lever ranking (sparse attention > capacitor mod > optimizer swap) and make the sparse-attention axis marginal rather than decisive. A third, cheaper falsifier: if the shipped NSA kernels are Hopper-only (as FlashMLA now is, sm_100a/sm_103a with Hopper explicitly dropped), then 'run NSA instead' is itself a porting project and the program has no runnable sparse-attention arm at all.
gaps.overturn_condition: An sm_80 DSA/CSA2 fwd+bwd kernel tested on A100; or a measured NSA end-to-end 32k training speedup <= 2x vs FlashAttention-2 on A100; or NSA's shipped kernels being Hopper-only.
gaps.evidence_tier_target: T2 (repo documentation / community measurement on A100 sm_80)

gaps.target_position: #5 - a 9B-token null is interpretable only as a bound, never a verdict; the fix is a 4-size ladder x 2 architectures at 1/3 budget (~12-35 days), not more tokens.
search_queries: scaling law fit architecture delta exceeds run-to-run noise 9B tokens 500M parameters
seed variance language model pretraining final loss standard deviation small scale 500M
Engram n-gram memory ablation token budget loss delta 10B tokens measured
gaps.rationale: The 'underpowered by 2-14x' claim rests on a 3.5%-relative noise floor borrowed from a scaling-law-estimation paper measured at 1B/100B (DataDecide) and on a ln(tokens) projection of 100B-token deltas down to 9B - a projection the locus itself rates low-confidence T4. Two sources would break it. (a) A measured seed-to-seed spread for LM pretraining at ~500M params and ~9-10B tokens, not at 1B/100B. If the spread is <=1% relative (<=0.03 nats), the memory axis's 0.014-0.082 nat deltas become detectable at 9B, the single-point A/B is viable after all, and the ladder recommendation is unnecessary. Candidate sources: Wortsman et al. 'Small-scale proxies for large-scale Transformer training instabilities' (many seeds at 100M-1B), reproducibility studies of small-scale LM pretraining, and DataDecide's own 3-seed variance at the 1B/5xC rung. (b) A measured memory-axis or attention-axis delta at <=10B tokens that is >=0.1 nats. The corpus already contains a near-miss the locus under-reads: MoBA's own smallest scaling-law point (568M/10.8B) has a measured 32K gap of 0.105 nats, i.e. 3.8% relative, which is at or above the 3.5% floor - not below it. The locus's 0.060-nat figure extrapolates below the smallest measured point in its own source. If the memory axis behaves the same way (Engram's capacity ablation is monotone at 5-10B tokens), a 9B run can see the effect and the 'null is the expected result' conclusion is wrong.
gaps.overturn_condition: A measured seed-to-seed spread <= 1% relative at ~500M params / ~9-10B tokens; or a measured architecture delta >= 0.1 nats at <=10B tokens for the memory or attention axis.
gaps.evidence_tier_target: T3 (published measurement) or T1 (two seeds on this box, ~14 days)

gaps.target_position: #6 - 0.75 GiB/s is the nccl-tests busbw column, not algbw; P2P is a latency lever, not a bandwidth lever; the 24-capacitor x16 mod is the only order-of-magnitude fabric lever but its value collapses once DDP overhead is ~4%.
search_queries: all_reduce_perf 5 ranks PCIe Gen2 x4 no P2P busbw algbw 1GB output CMP 170HX
CMP 170HX BAR1 P2P NCCL all-reduce working cmpunlocker RMForceStaticBar1 64MB BAR1
cmpunlocker P2P NCCL collective benchmark working 170HX 5 cards
gaps.rationale: The decisive artifact is the user's own `all_reduce_perf` output at 5 ranks, 1 MB / 100 MB / 1 GB, with both columns printed and the message size and rank count recorded - no corpus source can substitute for it, and the corpus's own club receipt is 3 cards at x16 behind PLX, not 5 cards at x4. Two readings would break the position. (a) If the user quoted the algbw column and it reads 0.75 GiB/s, the busbw reading is wrong: the fabric is then better than the corpus's 0.58-0.67 GB/s algbw band supports, which requires one traversal per hop, i.e. live P2P. (b) A working NCCL all-reduce over BAR1 P2P on a 64 MB-BAR1 GA100 at Gen2 x4 showing busbw >= 1.5 GB/s (vs ~1.0 host-staged) would flip 'P2P is a latency lever' to 'P2P is a bandwidth lever' by removing the second traversal, raising the algbw ceiling from ~0.6 to ~0.98 GiB/s and making the 0.75 GiB/s algbw reading physically available. The club's p2p.md reports the patch hangs every collective because `kbusIsPcieBar1P2PMappingSupported_GH100` needs a static BAR1 spanning the framebuffer while the 170HX has 64 MB, so a fix or a working receipt would be the break. Caveat the drafter must carry: under the corrected 56.8 s compute window, the algbw-vs-busbw question is narrative-only (4.4% either way); it becomes decisive only if cc-1 overturns the 88%-attention correction and the compute window falls back toward 7.4 s, at which point 36% vs 54-58% is the live question.
gaps.overturn_condition: The user's own all_reduce_perf output showing 0.75 GiB/s in the algbw column at 5 ranks; or a working NCCL collective over BAR1 P2P on a 64 MB-BAR1 GA100 at Gen2 x4 with busbw >= 1.5 GB/s.
gaps.evidence_tier_target: T1 (user's box) or T2 (community receipt on a 64 MB-BAR1 GA100)
